name: INDONESIA
lead: Indonesia is the world's biggest archipelago, with over 17,000 islands. It is wider than the USA. Volcanoes rumble under rainforests where orangutans swing through the trees. Ancient temples rise from rice terraces.
geo: Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire with 130 active volcanoes, more than any other country. Krakatoa's 1883 eruption was heard in Australia, 3,100 km away.
The islands stretch 5,100 km from east to west, about the distance from London to Tehran. Some have jungle mountains. Others are flat coral atolls.
animals: Sumatra is the only place where tigers, elephants, rhinos and orangutans share one rainforest. The Komodo dragon grows up to 3 m long and lives on only a few islands.
The Coral Triangle around eastern Indonesia has the richest sea life on Earth. It has 600+ kinds of coral and 3,000 kinds of fish.
culture: Indonesia has 300+ ethnic groups and 700 languages. Bahasa Indonesia unites them all at school. Wayang kulit shadow puppet shows can last all night.
Batik is cloth dyed in wax patterns. People wear it at weddings and offices. A gamelan orchestra plays bronze gongs that shimmer like a waterfall of notes.
history: Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms thrived here for a thousand years. Borobudur (c. 800 CE) is the world's largest Buddhist monument.
The Dutch ruled for three and a half centuries, drawn by nutmeg, pepper and cloves. Sukarno declared independence on 17 August 1945.
wows: Komodo dragons can sense prey up to 9 km away.
Borobudur's 2,672 relief panels would stretch over 6 km.
Indonesia grows about 75% of the world's nutmeg.
Its motto 'Bhinneka Tunggal Ika' means Unity in Diversity.
Indonesia is moving its capital to Nusantara in Borneo.

myths.fact: Orangutans are apes, not monkeys. They have no tail. Their name means 'person of the forest' in Malay.

myths.myth: Spices were once cheap and common
myths.fact: Nutmeg was so valuable that in 1667 the Dutch swapped Manhattan for tiny Run island.
